patch.value: Sign changes with ed25519 and enforce trusted keys on publication
Sign change ids using ed25519, configure a trusted-key file and validate signatures at the publication boundary. Preserve signature validity across rewrites that retain change identity.

verify --signatures checks trusted ed25519 signatures; configured serve and push refuse unsigned or untrusted changes before ref publication; malformed, revoked and tampered signatures fail closed; signing keys never enter history.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: Design: explicit sign command avoids implicit key access during commit/rewrite. Ed25519 signs a versioned domain-separated canonical payload binding stable change id, tree, author, message and sorted pm item links; parents and committer are excluded so ancestry-only rewrites preserve validity. Content-changing rewrites remove the attestation and require explicit signing. Receiver policy binds SHA-256 SPKI fingerprints to author email identities and has effective-time revocations. Administrative trust/revoke operations share the object-store write lease with push; policy is reloaded under ref locks immediately before the complete batch publishes. Both HTTP and filesystem publication use that boundary. Private key files must be external to the repository and errors never include key bytes.

Full unchanged-threshold coverage is running. verify --signatures reports all rows in a nonzero error on failure because the existing pm host cannot return a structured report together with a nonzero exit (documented pm-cli #826 limitation). value.text: Final publication timing review identified a scheduled-revocation boundary worth tightening: a key can reach its effective revocation time while other receiver preflights run after cryptographic verification. Retain the crypto/trust result under the writer lock and recheck effective revocations immediately after FileId lease checks, before the first ref write. Adding an actual transport regression with real lease checks delayed across a scheduled effective time. This also preserves lease-expiry checking after expensive cryptography.
